A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HierLoc work. Their main text, tables, equations, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.9 support reliable comparison despite reformatting and an added qualitative example.

before.justification: v1 reports original HierLoc benchmark results, component and hyperparameter ablations, inference-efficiency measurements, and geographic error analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a worked geolocation example showing the predicted hierarchical path and its localization error.

M1.justification: The entity construction, Lorentz embeddings, multimodal attention, GWH-InfoNCE objective, and FAISS-assisted hierarchical inference remain unchanged. The added beam-search visualization illustrates the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions train separate models on OSV5M and MediaEval’16 and evaluate on OSV5M, IM2GPS, IM2GPS3K, and YFCC4K. The new Peru street-view example illustrates existing geolocation coverage without introducing a distinct task or test scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark and efficiency comparisons, including SC Retrieval, RFM S2, LocDiff, and the Table 2 baselines. The flat per-level baseline and beam-width-one comparison discussed more explicitly in v2 already appear in v1’s Table 8.

E3.justification: The dataset splits, metrics, backbone configurations, 100k/10k sensitivity-study subset, and training settings are retained. Both specify batch size 16, learning rate 0.0002, five epochs, and inference beam width 10; the new case study uses the existing inference procedure.

E4.justification: v2 adds a qualitative beam-search case study in Figure 5 and Appendix A.9, tracing candidate refinement through country, region, subregion, and city. The component ablations, beam-width analysis, efficiency comparisons, and geographic error analyses already exist in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The existing island/non-island error distributions and descriptive statistics are retained without a change in reporting practice.

E6.justification: The added Figure 5 example reports the path Peru–Cusco–Provincia de Urubamba–Ollantaytambo and an 11.0 km localization error. Numerical results in Tables 1–15 and the retained empirical figures are unchanged, including OSV5M GeoScore 3963 and mean error 861 km.

T1.justification: The Lorentz-space definitions, exponential/logarithmic maps, loss equations, haversine derivation, weighting kernels, and inner-product search equivalence are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the same entity-centric formulation, hyperbolic representation, geographic contrastive loss, efficiency claims, and reported OSV5M improvements. The added illustration does not alter the scope of these central contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 expands the earlier observation about missing street-level entities into an explicit discretization limit imposed by 240k fixed entities and a tradeoff between regional interpretability and sub-kilometer accuracy. Appendix A.9 also interprets the new example as illustrating structured geographic inference.

D1.justification: v1’s Section 7 promises release of entity-construction, training, and evaluation code upon acceptance; v2 removes this commitment without supplying replacement access information. The implementation, preprocessing, hardware, hyperparameters, and training-time disclosures otherwise remain unchanged. This does not establish any change in actual external code availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 refines the comparison with geocell methods: v1 emphasizes Euclidean labels and hierarchy used mainly for partitioning or evaluation, whereas v2 emphasizes loss of hierarchical signals through single-level outputs. The cited works remain the same; Clark et al. (2023), mentioned by title in v2, was already cited as GeoDecoder.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized revisions to related work, ablation signposting, and limitations, and adds the Appendix A.9 walkthrough. The section organization and most prose remain intact. The author block, affiliations, contact information, and publication header are also updated.

P2.justification: The paper is reformatted throughout into the narrower ICLR layout, changing spacing, display sizes, and placement. Tables 4–8 are grouped near the ablation discussion instead of being scattered through discussion and references. A new multipanel Figure 5 is added, while earlier Figures 5–7 are retained as Figures 6–8. Some labels in the new figure are truncated.

improvement.justification: The explicit discretization tradeoff in Section 5, worked inference example in Appendix A.9, and better placement of ablation tables modestly improve clarity and transparency. The method and quantitative evidence remain unchanged. Removing the conditional code-release pledge weakens reproducibility commitments, and the new figure has truncated labels, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the limited explanatory gains.
